definition: Fraction of answerable questions (1-9) whose correct evidence (expected guideline section) appears among the top-3 post-rerank retrieved chunks.
Same as Recall@3, computed on the top-5 post-rerank retrieved chunks.

Fraction of answerable questions (1-9) whose generated answer was judged both correct and grounded (no hallucination) in the retrieved text. Judged automatically by a local LLM-as-judge (Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, a model separate from the generator to avoid self-judging bias, constrained to structured JSON output). Judge reliability was validated by cross-checking its verdicts against an independent cloud judge on a prior run: the cloud judge disagreed with a same-model self-judge's lenient verdicts on 6 of 9 questions (dev_logs.md Entry 14), which is why generator and judge are required to be different models here.
Fraction of trap questions (10-12, no answer exists in the corpus) correctly refused rather than confidently (and wrongly) answered.

Mean, over answerable questions, of 1/log2(rank+1) if the expected section appears at position `rank` in the top-5 post-rerank chunks, else 0. Unlike Recall@k, this rewards ranking the correct passage higher rather than treating every top-k position as equivalent -- included as an additional honest rate on ranking quality, not just hit/miss.
